name: Aegyo-sal highlighting

lead: Aegyo sal (Korean for roughly 'charm flesh') is the small roll of fullness just under the lower lash line, associated with a friendly, youthful look. Highlighting is the makeup approach to it: a pale or shimmery tone is placed on the roll and a soft shadow line underneath to make it appear more defined.

The appearance payoff is eyes that look softer, younger and more expressive in photos and in person. The technique is common in Korean and Japanese beauty trends, and there is no clinical research on it as a technique.

paras: Makeup users tap a light shimmer or champagne-toned product along the area directly beneath the lower lashes, and some add a faint shadow line beneath it to define the roll. Pencils and liquid products made for the purpose are sold in Korean and Japanese cosmetics lines. Results are visible immediately and wash off with makeup.

As a cosmetic applied near the eyes, the main considerations are product irritation and removing makeup safely, and the technique does not alter tissue. Fillers or surgery for the same area are separate procedures with their own entries.

angle.text: The makeup adds visible emphasis to the area under the lower lashes, which people use to make their eyes look friendlier and more youthful. It is a temporary cosmetic effect.

lead: Aegyo sal is the name for the slight fullness along the lower eyelid, below the lashes, that makes eyes look softer and gives a smile more of the eyes. The word aegyo itself denotes a cute, affectionate manner of speech and expression, widely expected of K-pop idols and younger women in Korean culture.[1]

Highlighting aegyo sal is a makeup practice: light, shimmery colour is applied to the roll, and a gentle line of shadow beneath it can add depth, creating the impression of larger, friendlier eyes. It is one of several Korean and Japanese eye-makeup trends aimed at a youthful look; related terms include the Japanese namidabukuro and the Chinese ruitai.
No clinical studies have examined the technique.
infobox: Lower eyelid, just beneath the lashes

paras: Aegyo sal refers to the fullness of the tissue under the lower lashes, noticeable most when smiling. The term draws on aegyo, the performance of cuteness through voice, expression and gesture, which scholars describe as a gendered behaviour expected especially of K-pop idols and young women.[1] Makeup that emphasises the roll is a visual shorthand for that youthful, approachable quality.
Highlighting appears in tutorials and product lines from Korean and Japanese brands, and the roll can also be approached through fillers or surgery, covered in separate entries.
